name: [Equip] Gemini calls are failing
query: sum(last_30m):sum:equip.gemini.calls_total{outcome:transport OR outcome:retry OR outcome:rate_limited OR outcome:unavailable OR outcome:rejected OR outcome:review_failed}.as_count() > 20
message:
The translation provider is refusing or timing out.

The provider retries transient failures itself (408/429/500/502/503/504, bounded), so this firing means the retries are not clearing it. Translations stop landing; nothing is lost — rows sit at `failed` and the sweep comes back for them — but a course being published now will sit in `publishing`, invisible to students, until it clears.

**Read the `outcome` tag on the alert; it is the whole diagnosis.**

* `rate_limited` — a 429. Money. Either the key's quota/prepaid balance, or a runaway loop of ours. Measured 2026-08-17, the key handled 1,626 requests/minute at width 16 without one refusal, so a real 429 storm is a change on Google's side or a loop on ours.
* `retry` — a 408 or a 5xx. Google is having a moment; it usually clears itself.
* `unavailable` — a shut door: 401 (key rejected), 403 (key disabled, billing off, project suspended), 404 (the model id no longer exists — check GEMINI_MODEL and GEMINI_REVIEW_MODEL against a deploy). Nothing translates until somebody acts.
* `rejected` — the API looked at one request and refused it: a block past the token ceiling, a payload it cannot parse. A property of the text, not of the service. The attempt cap handles it.
* `transport` — the call never landed. No HTTP status at all.
* `review_failed` — the reader, not the translator. Translations still ship, unread.

@arvavitcorp@gmail.com

NOTE ON THE QUERY. This used to add two series together — `sum:…{outcome:transport} + sum:…{outcome:retry}` — which reads correctly and does not work: Datadog aligns the two series before adding, so a timestamp present on one side and absent on the other produces no result at all. Both outcomes are rare (4 transport and 3 retry events in the 30 days to 2026-08-19), so in practice the addition would have been empty almost exactly when it mattered. A single query with an OR scope has no such join.

NOTE ON THE SCOPE. `fatal` used to be in here and no longer exists as a value. It merged a shut door with a refused payload — a disabled key and an oversized block counted as the same thing, and only one of them is fixed by editing the text. It is now `unavailable` and `rejected`, the split `translation/protocol.py` already draws between `TranslationUnavailable` and `TranslationError`. `rate_limited` and `review_failed` are new for the same reason: `status_code` on this metric is `N/A` on every series (the log-based-metric rule groups by `model` and `outcome` only, verified 2026-08-20), so a name that means two things can never be taken apart afterwards. `fatal` never fired in the 30 days before the rename, so no history is lost.
